plain_claim: For a source program in which no block reachable from the entry has an edge into the entry, whose assigned variables all lie in vars, with a phi placement equal to DF+ of each variable's definition points (entry included) and a renaming source that picks, at every reachable non-entry block without a phi for x, the nearest strictly dominating definition point of x (phis included), and an SSA initial store that holds each variable's initial value in its entry name: on every walk from the entry with last block b, (1) on entry to b every variable's source value equals the value of the SSA name the construction reads for an upward-exposed use at b, and (2) after b's body every variable's source value equals the value of its live-out SSA name at b. The acyclic corollary replaces the entry hypothesis by acyclicity.
statement: EntryNoReachablePreds S.cfg -> hvars -> hphi_cover -> hphi_within -> hidom -> hinit -> Walk S.cfg S.cfg.entry b path -> S.toProg.atTop sigma path x = (ssaConstruct S vars phi idom).atTop sigma' path (topName S phi idom x b) /\ S.toProg.run sigma path x = (ssaConstruct S vars phi idom).run sigma' path (liveOutName S phi idom x b)

hypotheses.purpose: The construction never puts phis at the entry; a reachable edge back into the entry needs one.
hypotheses.counterexample_class: the 1-node CFG with a self-loop on the entry

hypotheses.name: hacyc : Acyclic S.cfg (premise of ssaConstruct_preserves_values_of_acyclic, in place of hnp)
hypotheses.purpose: Acyclicity implies EntryNoReachablePreds (Toy.Ssa.entryNoReachablePreds_of_acyclic); the entry self-loop program, which is not acyclic, satisfies every other hypothesis of the corollary and its conclusion fails.
hypotheses.counterexample_class: the 1-node CFG with a self-loop on the entry

hypotheses.name: hvars : forall b x e, (x, e) in S.body b -> x in vars
hypotheses.purpose: Phis are emitted only for variables in vars.
hypotheses.counterexample_class: the diamond program with vars = []

hypotheses.name: hphi_cover : forall x b, IDF S.cfg (S.defPts x) b -> phi x b = true
hypotheses.purpose: A missing phi at a join leaves a stale value.
hypotheses.counterexample_class: the diamond program with no phis

hypotheses.name: hphi_within : forall x b, phi x b = true -> IDF S.cfg (S.defPts x) b
hypotheses.purpose: topName reads a phi name for every phi x b, but phis are emitted only for x in vars; a spurious phi for a variable outside vars is read uninitialized.
hypotheses.counterexample_class: the diamond program with a spurious phi for a variable outside vars

hypotheses.name: hidom : forall x b, Reachable S.cfg b -> b != S.cfg.entry -> phi x b = false -> NearestSDomDef S.cfg (fun d => S.defPts x d \/ phi x d = true) b (idom x b)
hypotheses.purpose: Renaming must read the nearest dominating definition.
hypotheses.counterexample_class: the 3-node chain program renamed to the entry value

hypotheses.name: hinit : forall x, sigma' (x, S.cfg.entry, 0) = sigma x
hypotheses.purpose: The SSA entry names hold the initial values.
hypotheses.counterexample_class: the diamond program with entry names initialized to 5

hypotheses.name: hw : Walk S.cfg S.cfg.entry b path
hypotheses.purpose: Executions start at the entry.
hypotheses.counterexample_class: the diamond program on the null walk at 3

nonvacuity_witness: Diamond program (x := x + 1 in block 1, phi at 3); a while loop with an unreachable block and renaming through the loop-header phi; an acyclic CFG whose entry has an unreachable predecessor (EntryNoPreds fails).
non_claims: Static single assignment of the output is a separate result (ssa-construct-single-assignment); strictness (every use dominated by its definition) is not stated or proved here.

The hypothesis hnp allows edges into the entry from unreachable blocks and from no reachable block; in an acyclic CFG every edge into the entry comes from an unreachable block (Toy.Ssa.entryNoReachablePreds_of_acyclic), which is why the acyclic corollary needs no entry hypothesis.

The tightness witness for hphi_within uses a variable outside vars (Toy.Ssa.ssaConstruct_needs_phi_within); whether extra phis for variables in vars (for example maximal placement at every non-entry block) also preserve values is not established here (not proved here).
Liveness-pruned placements, which drop phis inside DF+ for dead variables, violate hphi_cover and are not covered; neither are copy folding or later SSA optimizations.
Branch conditions are not modeled: every walk is an execution; a procedure exit is observed through conclusion (2) at the last block of a walk; there is no separate exit semantics.

Existence, for an arbitrary program, of a renaming source satisfying hidom is not proved here (not proved here); the non-vacuity witnesses exhibit one on concrete programs, including one with an unreachable block.
Not a model of LLVM mem2reg, Cranelift, or rustc; any such connection is a separate derived (modeling bridge) claim.

plain_claim: For every SSA program in which every predecessor of a block carrying phis has that block as its only successor, the naive translation with parallel copies satisfies, along every walk with last block b: (a) on entry to b (after b's phis in the SSA program) the two stores are equal on all variables, and (b) if no successor of b carries phis, the stores are also equal after b's body.
statement: PhiPredsSingleSucc P -> Walk P.cfg a b path -> (naiveOutOfSsa .parallel P).atTop sigma path = P.atTop sigma path /\ ((forall c, P.cfg.edge b c = true -> P.phis c = []) -> (naiveOutOfSsa .parallel P).run sigma path = P.run sigma path)

hypotheses.purpose: Copies for a phi block also run on the other branches of a branching predecessor.
hypotheses.counterexample_class: the lost-copy loop (critical back edge)

hypotheses.name: mode = .parallel
hypotheses.purpose: Sequential copies break when a phi reads another phi's destination.
hypotheses.counterexample_class: the swap loop

hypotheses.name: hw : Walk P.cfg a b path
hypotheses.purpose: On a non-walk, copies for a real successor are visible elsewhere.
hypotheses.counterexample_class: the swap CFG on the non-walk [0, 3]

hypotheses.name: hexit : forall c, P.cfg.edge b c = true -> P.phis c = [] (premise of conclusion (b) only)
hypotheses.purpose: At the end of a block with a phi-carrying successor the naive translation has already run that successor's copies.
hypotheses.counterexample_class: the 2-node lost-copy loop without an exit block

nonvacuity_witness: The swap loop (back edge split by a latch) on a walk ending at its exit block.
non_claims: Returns, halts, and exceptional exits must be modeled as edges to an explicit exit block: conclusion (b) is stated for the end of a block none of whose successors carries phis, and without an exit edge the naive translation's store at the end of a phi-predecessor differs (Toy.Ssa.naiveOutOfSsa_run_needs_exit; the exact relation, Toy.Ssa.naiveOutOfSsa_parallel_run_eq_outCopies, states that under PhiPredsSingleSucc, along every walk with last block b, the parallel naive translation's store at the end of b equals the SSA program's store there followed by outCopies .parallel P b, the copies appended to b).

Relaxing full-store equality to live variables would excuse phis at single-predecessor blocks whose destinations are dead on the other branch (not proved here), but not critical edges: lostSsa is already strict SSA with x2 live at the exit and still miscompiles (Toy.Ssa.lostCopy_naive_miscompiles); approaches that avoid edge splitting, such as conventional SSA (non-interfering phi-related live ranges) or saving live phi destinations in temporaries, are not formalized here (not proved here).

Assumes a simple CFG and omits branch instructions: parallel edges from p to b with different phi operands, and terminators at the end of p that read variables overwritten by the appended copies, are not modeled.
The naive translation appends the copies for all successors of p one after another; under PhiPredsSingleSucc all but at most one of them are empty.

A machine without a parallel-copy instruction executes a parallel copy as a sequence of moves (treated by naive-out-of-ssa-sequential-eq-of-seq-safe and swap-temp-sequence-correct); register allocation and coalescing are not covered.

tier_justification: The ordering condition for sequential copies (Briggs et al. Figure 13; parallel-move sequentialization) made precise for the naive translation.
plain_claim: For every SSA program in which every predecessor of a block carrying phis has that block as its only successor and in which, for every pair of blocks (p, b) (including non-edges, since SsaProg.phis supplies total operand functions), no phi destination of b is the destination or the p-operand of a later phi of b (SeqSafe (P.phiMoves p b)), the naive translation with sequential copies in phi order satisfies conclusions (a) and (b) of the parallel theorem along every walk. At the level of one move list: SeqSafe moves executed one at a time have the effect of the parallel copy.

non_claims: The hypothesis hs is not guarded by P.cfg.edge p b = true: it requires SeqSafe (P.phiMoves p b) for every pair of blocks (p, b), including pairs that are not CFG edges, for which SsaProg.phis still supplies operands (SsaProg.phis b : List (V × (Fin n → V)) gives each phi a total operand function). Whether the conclusion still holds when hs is restricted to CFG edges (P.cfg.edge p b = true) is not established here (not proved here).
SeqSafe is a sufficient condition; whether a weaker condition suffices (for example, when the values of the reordered copies happen to coincide) is not examined (not proved here).

Distinct phi destinations are part of SeqSafe and cannot be dropped: two phis for the same destination give the first operand under parallel copies but the last under sequential copies (Toy.Ssa.dupPhi_sequential_wrong).

A phi order can be SeqSafe even when another order of the same phis is not (Toy.Ssa.chainPhi_order_matters); cyclic copies such as the swap admit no SeqSafe order, because the first move of any order writes a source of a later move (not proved here as a general theorem; the swap list [(0, 1), (1, 0)] is shown not SeqSafe in Toy.Ssa.execBody_sequential_needs_seqSafe).

Returns, halts, and exceptional exits must be modeled as edges to an explicit exit block: conclusion (b) is stated for the end of a block none of whose successors carries phis, and without an exit edge the naive translation's store at the end of a phi-predecessor differs (Toy.Ssa.naiveOutOfSsa_run_needs_exit for parallel copies and Toy.Ssa.naiveOutOfSsa_sequential_run_needs_exit for sequential copies; the exact relation, Toy.Ssa.naiveOutOfSsa_parallel_run_eq_outCopies, states that under PhiPredsSingleSucc, along every walk with last block b, the parallel naive translation's store at the end of b equals the SSA program's store there followed by outCopies .parallel P b, the copies appended to b).

tier_justification: Briggs et al.'s swap problem as a concrete kernel-checked instance.
plain_claim: On the swap loop (a1 := 1, b1 := 2; header phis a2 = phi(a1, b2), b2 = phi(b1, a2); back edge split by a latch block), after one back-edge traversal the SSA program has (a2, b2) = (2, 1), while the naive translation with sequential copies gives (2, 2) in phi order [a2, b2] and (1, 1) in phi order [b2, a2].
statement: (swapSsaAB.atTop 0 swapWalk 2, swapSsaAB.atTop 0 swapWalk 3) = (2, 1) /\ (swapSsaBA ...) = (2, 1) /\ ((naiveOutOfSsa .sequential swapSsaAB).atTop 0 swapWalk 2, ... 3) = (2, 2) /\ ((naiveOutOfSsa .sequential swapSsaBA).atTop 0 swapWalk 2, ... 3) = (1, 1), with swapWalk = [0, 1, 2, 1] and variables a1 = 0, b1 = 1, a2 = 2, b2 = 3
nonvacuity_witness: Concrete instance.
non_claims: Sequential copies in phi order do realize the parallel copy of one move list when no destination in the list is the destination or the source of a later move (SeqSafe, Toy.Ssa.execBody_sequential_eq_parCopy); combined with PhiPredsSingleSucc, SeqSafe of the phi moves for every pair of blocks (p, b), including pairs that are not CFG edges, makes the sequential naive translation exact (naive-out-of-ssa-sequential-eq-of-seq-safe). Without distinct destinations this fails (Toy.Ssa.dupPhi_sequential_wrong), and without PhiPredsSingleSucc it fails even with a single phi, whose moves are SeqSafe for every pair of blocks (Toy.Ssa.naiveOutOfSsa_sequential_needs_phiPredsSingleSucc).

Does not imply that every cyclic copy needs a temporary: on one instance where a cycle vertex also feeds a destination outside the cycle, (a2, b2, c2) := (b2, a2, a2), three plain assignments suffice (Toy.Ssa.windmill_sequential_no_temp); hardware exchange instructions are not modeled.
With a1 = b1 both orders would give the right values, so the failure depends on the input values (not proved here).

plain_claim: On Briggs et al.'s lost-copy loop (CFG 0 -> 1, 1 -> 1, 1 -> 2; x1 := 1; x2 = phi(x1, x3); x3 := x2 + 1; the exit reads x2), on the walk [0, 1, 1, 2] the source returns 2 and the SSA program has x2 = 2 at the exit, but the naive translation has x2 = 3 with parallel copies and with sequential copies.
statement: lostSource.atTop 0 lostWalk 1 = 2 /\ lostSsa.atTop 0 lostWalk 1 = 2 /\ (naiveOutOfSsa .parallel lostSsa).atTop 0 lostWalk 1 = 3 /\ (naiveOutOfSsa .sequential lostSsa).atTop 0 lostWalk 1 = 3, with lostWalk = [0, 1, 1, 2] and variables x1 = 0, x2 = 1, x3 = 2
nonvacuity_witness: Concrete instance.
non_claims: The miscompilation is exhibited on one program with a critical back edge and a folded copy, and splitting that edge removes it (lost-copy-split-fixes); it is not a claim that every critical edge causes one, and which features of the program are necessary for it is not examined (not proved here).

plain_claim: For every number k of back-edge traversals (the loop body runs k + 1 >= 1 times) and every initial store, the naive parallel-copy translation of the lost-copy program on the CFG with the critical edge 1 -> 1 split by a new block 3 reaches the exit with the same store as the SSA program on the original CFG.

nonvacuity_witness: Both compared lists are walks for every k (lostLoopWalk_walk, lostSplitWalk_walk).
